title: Our Rabbis in the South
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies them as Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, as in Yevamot 62b.
In the generations of the first Amoraim, Hyman identifies the designation with Rabbi Afes and cites Eruvin 62b.

notes.text: The William Davidson digital text of Yevamot 62b explicitly lists Elazar ben Shamua among Akiva’s five southern students, supporting that expansion of ראבר״ש; the alternative Elazar son of Shimon remains a possible literal expansion of the abbreviation. The Afes identification at Eruvin 62b remains unverified: the saved named paragraph does not confirm it, and the reviewer’s broader nonmatch report is preserved without asserting a new root whole-folio absence.

The matching exchange appears in the consulted Eruvin at 65b. Reish Lakish proposes that they rent now and consult “our Rabbis in the South” when they arrive. They later ask Rabbi Afes, who approves what they did. Hyman cites 62b in this entry and 65b for the same exchange in his separate entry on Reish Lakish (vol. III, p. 1196).
